sources.title: Built on official & public information
sources.sub: MINFO answers only from a curated set of official and public organizations. Every answer links back to them.

roadmap.title: Tokyo Open Data Catalog connection
roadmap.body: Link answers to live public datasets (facilities, consultation desks, disaster info) instead of static entries.

roadmap.title: Ward-by-ward expansion
roadmap.body: The category + source structure is ward-agnostic: swap in each ward's official pages to cover all of Tokyo.

roadmap.title: Anonymized question trends
roadmap.body: Understand what information residents actually need, shared with wards as a public-interest signal, never as personal data.

openData.title: From open data to usable guidance
openData.sub: Open data becomes useful when residents can find it, understand it, and act on it. MINFO builds that final mile.

now.body: {count} curated records from official/public sources power every answer and source card. Hand-checked, structured open-data-ready.

next.body: Tokyo / Shinjuku open datasets are identified below, prioritized by usefulness and update needs. Automatic fetching is future work.

openData.strategyTitle: How MINFO chooses a data access method
openData.strategyIntro: Not every dataset should be a live API. The method follows how fast the information changes:

strategy.title: Stable information
strategy.body: Rules and contact desks that rarely change. Curated CSV/JSON source records are enough for the MVP.

strategy.title: Periodically updated data
strategy.body: Facility lists and statistics. Scheduled CSV downloads or batch updates can refresh these records.

strategy.title: Time-sensitive information
strategy.body: Disasters, shelter status, sudden closures. Future versions may need APIs or frequent automated updates.

openData.candidatesSub: Catalog entries and search targets MINFO plans to connect next, with what each would improve. None are fetched automatically yet.

quality.title: MINFO source-quality check
quality.sub: A lightweight checklist inspired by Japan's public open-data quality guidance, not a formal government assessment. Every source in MINFO goes through it.

items.label: Official / public source
items.desc: Published by a government body or public organization.

items.label: Link verified
items.desc: The URL was checked by hand and points to the official page.

items.label: Language accessible
items.desc: Multilingual, or usable with simple Japanese.

items.label: Daily-life relevance
items.desc: Answers a question residents actually ask.

items.label: Update-ready
items.desc: The record can be refreshed when the source changes.

items.label: Ward-expandable
items.desc: The same structure can host other wards' sources.

items.label: Improved by feedback
items.desc: User feedback can flag and fix weak sources.

whyMinfo.title: Why MINFO, not just search or AI chat?
whyMinfo.sub: MINFO is not trying to beat search engines or general AI at general knowledge. It does one local job well.

cards.title: Search engines
cards.body: Give you many links. You still have to judge which page is official, current, and applies to Shinjuku.

cards.title: General AI chat
cards.body: Gives broad, general answers. Helpful, but not grounded in your ward's offices, and it can guess.

cards.title: MINFO
cards.body: Local, source-grounded next steps in your language, with official sources on every answer and 119/110 guidance that never changes. A navigator to real offices, never a replacement for them.

story.title: Why Shinjuku / Okubo?
story.sub: A civic-tech pilot for multilingual information access, designed to expand across Tokyo.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.body: Official life information in Japan is reliable, but scattered across dozens of sites, written in dense administrative Japanese, and hard to act on. For residents navigating an unfamiliar system in a second language, even simple questions ("which counter?", "which form?") become barriers.

blocks.title: The people
blocks.body: Foreign-origin residents and multilingual communities: newly arrived residents, international students, workers, families, and the community supporters who help them. People facing language and information-access barriers, not a lack of ability.

blocks.title: The approach
blocks.body: MINFO is not a translation chatbot. It is a civic information navigator: it explains daily-life systems simply, in six languages including やさしい日本語, always shows its official sources, and guides people to the right real-world office, never replacing it.

blocks.title: Pilot → expansion
blocks.body: Shinjuku / Okubo is the pilot: one of Japan's most visibly multilingual neighborhoods, dense with students, workers, and families who need daily-life information. The same category + trusted-source structure can then roll out ward by ward across Tokyo.

impact: Healthcare access in your own language
Garbage, tax, and housing rules made clear
Consultation desks that people actually find
